method: Root visually inspects each actual original before reading its final gate statuses, then compares the exact contracts and keeps any limitation explicit. Record audit does not infer pixels.

observations.inspection: original pixels via view_image detail original
observations.blind_whole_scene_reading: A woman steadies a green seedling tray on a high wooden shelf in a wet coastal work room. Her two arms and the tray contacts connect into a readable task. Window light, a water-stained wall, muddy floor, equipment and other plant trays give the practical scene context. Her face is prominent and turned toward the camera; the image reads as a carefully arranged, softly lit work portrait.
observations.reference_scope: Dark chin-length bob, separated fine fringe, dark eyes, pink lips and visible facial contours follow the supplied face/hair guidance. This is qualitative visible guidance, not identity or body-similarity proof.
observations.selected_relation_observation: The charcoal band is visibly separate from the ivory blouse panels, follows the same worn blouse waist and meets the visible front tied bow. The tray stays to the side of the waist so its main band and tie are readable together.
observations.support_observation: The tray bottom is aligned with and rests on the exposed shelf. Both hands meet its rim and connect through wrists, elbows and shoulders to the one main subject. Actual load magnitude is not measured.
limitations: Both boot soles and their contact with the grate are below the saved image boundary. The authored just-below-boots framing is not fully realized.
The hidden foot contacts, exact grate material, fiber identity and the historical cause/time of the water traces are not proven by this image.
observations.scope_assessment: The inherited/research focal relation is the same-blouse waist band and visible tie; no ordinary candidate or whole-route/count bundle adds a foot-contact duty. The shelf-supported tray is the consequential action load. Incidental off-frame foot support is a disclosed framing deviation and is not promoted to a new universal gate.

observations.inspection: Original via view_image detail original and exact unresampled native hand/buckle and coat/flank crops. No interpolation used as proof.
observations.blind_whole_scene_reading: Two people share a practical buckle task at a station bench. The main subject is fully seated with both loafers on the floor and the case is beside her on the bench. A man lifts the case strap and steadies its top handle; the woman has both hands around a black buckle.
observations.reference_scope: Visible dark short bob, fine fringe, softly tapered facial contours and pink lips follow the face/hair guidance qualitatively. Downward gaze differs from the reference camera gaze. Identity and body similarity are not asserted.
observations.selected_relation_observation: Both shoulder-strap attachment fittings are visibly attached to this same case, with the strap route lifted above them. The long coat is open in front and beside the knees, but the required torso-side gap at waist is hidden by the coat-covered forearm and adjoining fabric.
observations.mechanism_observation: The buckle housing and mated center are recognizable, but the rigid tongue fork tips are concealed and the buckle appears already joined. This does not show the frozen guiding-tongue-into-housing interaction state.
observations.support_observation: The main soles and their floor contact, bench/seat support and case/bench support are visible. Arms and hands form coherent connected chains.

required_failure_observations.reason: Torso-side gap owner/endpoints are obscured; front opening and hem gap cannot substitute.
Closed mated buckle conceals the distinct tongue entering the housing.

observations.targeted_endpoint_recheck: Reopened the unresampled first bag_route crop after the A2 endpoint ambiguity. In A1 the right post-grip broad webbing visibly continues over the bag corner into its outer metal clip/fitting, separately from the top carry-handle curve. The first carrier assignment remains supported. The A2 failure is missing/ambiguous endpoint ownership, not a universal demand that every pixel of the strap route be unoccluded by a grip.

observations.inspection: Saved original pixels via view_image detail original, before agent final gate results.
observations.blind_whole_scene_reading: A close photographic hat repair at a wooden table. A woman holds a silver needle at its shaft and pins the hat ribbon with the other hand. A gold thread joins the exposed needle-eye region to a visible fresh ribbon stitch. Face and hands dominate the image; a chair, tabletop, scissors and thread spool give the work setting.
observations.reference_scope: Dark chin-length bob, fine separated fringe, dark eyes, facial contours, straight visible nose and softly full pink lips follow the supplied face/hair guidance. Identity or body similarity are not asserted.
observations.mechanism_observation: The principal needle grip, separated metal shaft, exposed eye region, thread route and ribbon contact can be followed across one readable plane. Actual thread fiber, tension and temporal motion are not measured.
observations.selected_relation_observation: The exposed wrist cuff belongs to a chunky looped knit garment with ribbed/rolled boundary. It does not expose resolved fine yarn crossings together with a separate sewing-stitch edge on the same patch. Fine texture on the hat ribbon cannot substitute for the declared jacket cuff owner.

required_failure_observations.reason: The native cuff shows coarse loops/knit and boundary rather than both fine crossings and distinct sewing stitches in one cloth patch.

mechanism_limitations: The pointed needle tip is under the gripping fingers. The visible shaft/eye/thread/stitch chain is supported, but the complete frozen recognition assertion including a pointed tip is not fully observed.

observations.inspection: Saved original via view_image detail original before the final agent gate statuses.
observations.blind_whole_scene_reading: A close repair portrait at a wooden table. The main face and hair are prominent; one hand holds a silver needle and the other pins a black ribbon to a straw-appearing broad-brimmed hat. A continuous gold thread leads from the visible eye to the ribbon stitch.
observations.reference_scope: The supplied dark short bob, fine separated fringe, dark eyes, facial contours and pink lips remain qualitatively supported. No actual identity, age or body similarity is asserted.
observations.selected_relation_observation: The exposed nearer cuff now displays fine crossing yarn lines across the same cloth surface immediately beside a separate seam/stitch row. It is distinguishable from the broad hat-body weave and black ribbon texture. WK047 appears completely realized on the declared cuff owner.
observations.mechanism_observation: The shaft extends from the gripping fingers toward a exposed oval eye. The thread and fresh stitch can be traced. The opposite pointed tip does not project beyond the grip: the shaft starts under the fingers. The complete frozen needle recognition/endpoint assertion is still not observed.
appearance_deviations: The hat body now appears straw-woven instead of the felt appearance in native_01. This is disclosed separately from whether that precise material was a mandatory inherited/requested/adopted field.

required_failure_observations.reason: The declared pointed endpoint of the major needle structure is hidden under the grip; eye/shaft alone cannot supply complete endpoint proof.

observations.additional_original_inspection: Reopened the same original and the agent-authored far_arm_and_hand native crop after a reported full-arm-chain limitation. No interpolation or extra image call.
observations.body_chain_limitation: The left pinning hand is visible, but its wrist, forearm and bent elbow path to the visible left shoulder is concealed behind the hat and right frame boundary. The frozen/precomposition promise of both complete working arm chains is not wholly observable. This is an evidence failure, not a conclusion of malformed anatomy.

observations.inspection: Original via view_image detail original before final gate statuses, followed by the unresampled hands_buckle and coat_flank crops.
observations.blind_whole_scene_reading: The main woman sits on a station bench with both loafers on the stone floor. The black case rests beside her. A standing man holds its raised shoulder strap and steadies its separate handle. The woman holds a black buckle with visible fork/latch-like branches between her two hands.
observations.reference_scope: Dark short bob, fine fringe, facial contours and pink lips qualitatively follow the supplied face/hair guidance. Her gaze is downward; actual identity, age and body similarity are not asserted.
observations.selected_relation_observation: Two metal fittings are visible on the same case, but the raised shoulder strap right return disappears under the helper gripping hand. The lower D-ring also serves the separate carry handle and the outer right clip has no directly traceable connection to the raised arch. The complete same-strap/same-case endpoint assignment is unobserved. Coat front opening remains visible, but the required torso-side clearance cannot be traced separately.
observations.mechanism_observation: Several fork/latch-like branches are more exposed than in attempt01. At native scale their role as actual tips entering an exposed housing mouth rather than external parts of a mated buckle is not yet unambiguously established. Preserve this ambiguity in the complete interaction-state judgment.
observations.support_observation: Both main soles meet the floor. The bench supports the seated body and the case. The main arm/sleeve chains and the helper hands keep their ownership visible.

required_failure_observations.reason: The required torso-side owners and their continuous waist-level gap cannot be directly distinguished from the visible front opening and cloth/lining.
The right strap-to-case endpoint connection is concealed. Do not assign carry-handle hardware or a separate outer clip to the raised shoulder strap without direct evidence.

observations.superseded_initial_attachment_observatio: Both metal strap attachment fittings belong to the same black case and are visible with the raised strap route. The coat is open in front; its near working arm covers the torso-side region. A continuous waist-level torso-side clearance bounded separately by the torso and coat side panel is not clearly traceable. The front aperture or dark fabric/lining cannot substitute.
observations.additional_original_inspection: Reopened bag_route and right_strap_endpoint unresampled crops after the carrier-assignment concern. Compared the unchanged WK080 native gate requiring the declared owner, both endpoints and connecting edge/state. A fitting count alone is insufficient; no universal whole-route gate added.
